1	# Feature Specification: P-RF05 — Personal summary export
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `010-personal-summary-export` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-10-24
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	## Clarifications
10	
11	### Session 2026-10-24
12	
13	- Q: What should the export sheet show when the job fails entirely (FR-007 — no data produced at all, not just the AI narrative), given the prototype only defines an "Erro" state for the narrative-only failure and has no visual for this harder case? → A: Generic failure message (reusing the error color/icon family, with copy distinct from FR-006's narrative-only explanation), no PDF/raw buttons, and only the existing "Fechar" link — no dedicated in-sheet retry control, and the same text is shown regardless of the backend's specific errorCode. Retrying means closing the sheet and tapping the download icon again (FR-011's existing path) (resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I).
14	
15	**Input**: User description: "P-RF05 — Personal summary export: Let the user export a narrative summary of their entries as PDF, and always be able to download the raw data. Requirement and acceptance criteria: docs/input/requirements.md, section 1, RF05. Prototype states: the export sheet — 'Pendente', 'Processando', 'Concluído', 'Erro', 'Período vazio' (prototype extract, section 2.5); opened by the download icon of Meus Registros. Screen ↔ job status mapping: docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md. Backend: POST /export/summary, GET /export/:jobId/status, GET /export/:jobId/download. Depends on: RF07. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements, section 2), or change the backend."
16	
17	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
18	
19	### User Story 1 - Getting a narrative PDF of your entries (Priority: P1)
20	
21	From My Records, the user taps the download icon and asks to export a summary of their entries. They watch the export prepare and then generate an AI narrative, and end up with a PDF they can download that tells the story of that period, alongside their original entries.
22	
23	**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF05 — a narrative export is the feature's main value. Without it reaching a downloadable PDF, the feature does not exist.
24	
25	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening the export sheet for a period that has at least one entry, letting the job run to completion, and confirming a PDF download succeeds and contains a narrative summary.
26	
27	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
28	
29	1. **Given** the user is on My Records with at least one entry in the exported period, **When** they tap the download icon, **Then** the export sheet opens and shows "Pendente" (spinner, "Preparando exportação...").
30	2. **Given** the export sheet is showing "Pendente", **When** the backend starts generating the AI narrative, **Then** the sheet shows "Processando" ("Gerando resumo com IA...", progress bar) without the user doing anything further.
31	3. **Given** the job finishes with both the data and the narrative ready, **When** the sheet updates, **Then** it shows "Concluído" (green check, "Resumo pronto") with two enabled buttons — "Baixar PDF" (primary) and "Baixar dados brutos" (outline).
32	4. **Given** the sheet is showing "Concluído", **When** the user taps "Baixar PDF", **Then** the app downloads a PDF file containing the generated narrative summary for that period.
33	
34	---
35	
36	### User Story 2 - Your raw data is never held hostage by the AI narrative (Priority: P1)
37	
38	Generating the narrative summary can fail — the AI call can time out or error out. When that happens, the user can still get their own data out: the export sheet explains that only the narrative failed and lets them download their raw entries anyway.
39	
40	**Why this priority**: Called out explicitly as its own acceptance criterion ("a failure generating the narrative text still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure"). Without this, a flaky AI call would make a user's own data unreachable, which is a trust-breaking failure for a personal-data feature.
41	
42	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by forcing the narrative generation to fail (e.g., simulating an AI timeout) for a period that does have entries, and confirming the sheet still offers — and completes — a raw-data download.
43	
44	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
45	
46	1. **Given** the export job's data finished successfully but the narrative generation failed or was skipped, **When** the sheet updates, **Then** it shows "Erro" (red warning) with text explaining that the AI summary failed but the data remains available, and exactly one enabled button — "Baixar dados brutos" (no "Baixar PDF" option is shown).
47	2. **Given** the sheet is showing this "Erro" state, **When** the user taps "Baixar dados brutos", **Then** the download succeeds with the user's raw entry data, with no dependency on the narrative ever having completed.
48	3. **Given** the export job fails entirely (not only the narrative — no data was produced either), **When** the sheet updates, **Then** it shows a failure state with no download option at all, which is visibly a harder failure than the narrative-only case in Scenario 1 (nothing is available to download because nothing was produced).
49	
50	---
51	
52	### User Story 3 - Exporting a period with nothing in it is handled gracefully (Priority: P2)
53	
54	The user requests an export for a period that turns out to have zero entries. Instead of an empty or broken PDF, or the app hanging, they get a clear message telling them there is nothing to export.
55	
56	**Why this priority**: Called out explicitly as an acceptance criterion ("an export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state — not an empty PDF, not a crash"). It is a correctness guarantee as much as a UX one.
57	
58	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by requesting an export for a period known to contain zero entries and confirming the sheet shows the dedicated empty-period state immediately, with no job ever appearing to run and no file ever offered for download.
59	
60	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
61	
62	1. **Given** the user selects a period with zero entries, **When** they request the export, **Then** the sheet shows "Período vazio" ("Nenhum registro nesse período." plus a suggestion to adjust the filter) directly — never "Pendente" or "Processando" first — and offers no download button.
63	2. **Given** the sheet is showing "Período vazio", **When** the user taps "Fechar", **Then** the sheet dismisses without having created any downloadable file and without affecting My Records' own list or filters.
64	
65	---
66	
67	### Edge Cases
68	
69	- The user taps "Fechar" while the job is still "Pendente" or "Processando": the sheet dismisses and the in-flight job is left alone server-side; the app does not keep polling it in the background once the sheet is gone, and it is not treated as the "current" export if the sheet is reopened.
70	- The user taps the download icon again while an export sheet/job from a previous tap is still in flight for the same period: this does not create a second concurrent export job — the tap is treated as a no-op (or reopens the same in-flight sheet) rather than firing a second `POST /export/summary`.
71	- The session expires while the export sheet is open: the existing expired-session overlay (RF07) takes over exactly as it does for the rest of the screen; once re-authenticated, the sheet resumes reflecting the export job's real status rather than being stuck mid-attempt.
72	- The download itself (PDF or raw data) fails after the job reached a downloadable state (e.g., the signed URL expired or the connection drops mid-download): the corresponding button returns to a retryable state rather than leaving the sheet stuck or silently failing.
73	- Opening the export sheet, polling its job, or downloading a file does not alter My Records' list, its active filters, its sync badges, or its scroll position in any way.
74	- Opening My Records itself, its filters, its tags, the chat, the dashboard, or any other screen or action not named in this feature: unaffected by this unit and not touched by it.
75	
76	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
77	
78	### Functional Requirements
79	
80	- **FR-001**: A download icon in My Records' header MUST open the export bottom sheet.

84	- **FR-005**: When the job's data and narrative both complete successfully, the sheet MUST show "Concluído" with two enabled controls — "Baixar PDF" (primary) and "Baixar dados brutos" (outline).
85	- **FR-006**: When the job's data completes but the narrative generation fails or is skipped, the sheet MUST show "Erro" with text explaining that the AI summary failed while the data remains available, and exactly one enabled control — "Baixar dados brutos" — with no PDF option offered.

87	- **FR-008**: "Baixar PDF" MUST only ever be offered when FR-005's conditions hold, and tapping it MUST download a PDF containing the generated narrative for the exported period.
88	- **FR-009**: "Baixar dados brutos" MUST be offered in both the FR-005 and FR-006 outcomes, and tapping it MUST download the user's raw entry data for the exported period, independent of whether the narrative ever succeeded.
89	- **FR-010**: A "Fechar" link MUST be present and functional in every one of the six sheet states ("Pendente", "Processando", "Concluído", "Erro" [FR-006's narrative-only failure], the full-failure state [FR-007], and "Período vazio"), dismissing the sheet without cancelling any in-flight backend job and without affecting My Records' own list, filters, or scroll position.

95	
96	- **Export Job**: An ephemeral, user-scoped job created by one export request, covering one period of entries. 101

103	- **SC-002**: In 100% of forced narrative-failure cases (for a period with entries), the user still completes a raw-data download from the same sheet, with a clear explanation of what happened.
104	- **SC-003**: Exporting a period with zero entries is communicated through a single, clear sheet state in 100% of tested cases, with zero downloadable files ever produced and zero crashes.
105	- **SC-004**: Closing the export sheet, from any of its five states, leaves My Records' list, active filters, and scroll position completely unchanged in 100% of tested cases.
106	- **SC-005**: No export attempt — successful, narrative-failed, fully failed, or empty-period — ever leaves the sheet showing a "preparing" or "generating" indicator indefinitely; every attempt reaches one of its defined terminal states within the system's normal response time.
107

109	
110	- **Period selection**: The export sheet exports whatever period My Records' own active date filter currently represents (or the entire history, if no date filter is applied) rather than offering a separate period picker inside the sheet itself — the prototype's export sheet shows no period-selection control of its own, and My Records already owns date filtering (RF06/RF07).
111	- **Narrative inclusion**: Every export request includes the narrative by default (there is no prototype control to opt out of it upfront) — a request only ends up "without narrative" when generation fails or is skipped, never by the user's deliberate choice.
112	- **When downloads become available**: The two download buttons appear only once the job reaches one of the sheet's defined terminal states — "Concluído" or "Erro" — matching the prototype's literal five-state catalog. 113	- **Full job failure vs. narrative-only failure**: These are treated as two distinct outcomes (see FR-006 vs. FR-007) because the backend distinguishes them (an overall failed job produces no data at all, so there is nothing to download) — the prototype's single "Erro" state is understood to describe the narrative-only failure specifically, since its own text says the data remains available.

115	- **File handling on download**: "Baixar PDF" and "Baixar dados brutos" trigger the platform's standard way of saving or sharing a downloaded file; this unit is not responsible for building a custom in-app file viewer.
116	- **Status polling**: The exact interval at which the sheet checks `GET /export/:jobId/status` while "Pendente"/"Processando" is an implementation detail, not a product requirement, as long as it is frequent enough that the user does not perceive the sheet as stuck.

# Feature Specification: P-RF05 — Personal summary export

**Feature Branch**: `010-personal-summary-export` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)

**Created**: 2026-10-24

**Status**: Draft

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-10-24

- Q: What should the export sheet show when the job fails entirely (FR-007 — no data produced at all, not just the AI narrative), given the prototype only defines an "Erro" state for the narrative-only failure and has no visual for this harder case? → A: Generic failure message (reusing the error color/icon family, with copy distinct from FR-006's narrative-only explanation), no PDF/raw buttons, and only the existing "Fechar" link — no dedicated in-sheet retry control, and the same text is shown regardless of the backend's specific errorCode. Retrying means closing the sheet and tapping the download icon again (FR-011's existing path) (resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I).

**Input**: User description: "P-RF05 — Personal summary export: Let the user export a narrative summary of their entries as PDF, and always be able to download the raw data. Requirement and acceptance criteria: docs/input/requirements.md, section 1, RF05. Prototype states: the export sheet — 'Pendente', 'Processando', 'Concluído', 'Erro', 'Período vazio' (prototype extract, section 2.5); opened by the download icon of Meus Registros. Screen ↔ job status mapping: docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md. Backend: POST /export/summary, GET /export/:jobId/status, GET /export/:jobId/download. Depends on: RF07. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements, section 2), or change the backend."

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Getting a narrative PDF of your entries (Priority: P1)

From My Records, the user taps the download icon and asks to export a summary of their entries. They watch the export prepare and then generate an AI narrative, and end up with a PDF they can download that tells the story of that period, alongside their original entries.

**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF05 — a narrative export is the feature's main value. Without it reaching a downloadable PDF, the feature does not exist.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening the export sheet for a period that has at least one entry, letting the job run to completion, and confirming a PDF download succeeds and contains a narrative summary.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user is on My Records with at least one entry in the exported period, **When** they tap the download icon, **Then** the export sheet opens and shows "Pendente" (spinner, "Preparando exportação...").
2. **Given** the export sheet is showing "Pendente", **When** the backend starts generating the AI narrative, **Then** the sheet shows "Processando" ("Gerando resumo com IA...", progress bar) without the user doing anything further.
3. **Given** the job finishes with both the data and the narrative ready, **When** the sheet updates, **Then** it shows "Concluído" (green check, "Resumo pronto") with two enabled buttons — "Baixar PDF" (primary) and "Baixar dados brutos" (outline).
4. **Given** the sheet is showing "Concluído", **When** the user taps "Baixar PDF", **Then** the app downloads a PDF file containing the generated narrative summary for that period.

---

### User Story 2 - Your raw data is never held hostage by the AI narrative (Priority: P1)

Generating the narrative summary can fail — the AI call can time out or error out. When that happens, the user can still get their own data out: the export sheet explains that only the narrative failed and lets them download their raw entries anyway.

**Why this priority**: Called out explicitly as its own acceptance criterion ("a failure generating the narrative text still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure"). Without this, a flaky AI call would make a user's own data unreachable, which is a trust-breaking failure for a personal-data feature.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by forcing the narrative generation to fail (e.g., simulating an AI timeout) for a period that does have entries, and confirming the sheet still offers — and completes — a raw-data download.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the export job's data finished successfully but the narrative generation failed or was skipped, **When** the sheet updates, **Then** it shows "Erro" (red warning) with text explaining that the AI summary failed but the data remains available, and exactly one enabled button — "Baixar dados brutos" (no "Baixar PDF" option is shown).
2. **Given** the sheet is showing this "Erro" state, **When** the user taps "Baixar dados brutos", **Then** the download succeeds with the user's raw entry data, with no dependency on the narrative ever having completed.
3. **Given** the export job fails entirely (not only the narrative — no data was produced either), **When** the sheet updates, **Then** it shows a failure state with no download option at all, which is visibly a harder failure than the narrative-only case in Scenario 1 (nothing is available to download because nothing was produced).

---

### User Story 3 - Exporting a period with nothing in it is handled gracefully (Priority: P2)

The user requests an export for a period that turns out to have zero entries. Instead of an empty or broken PDF, or the app hanging, they get a clear message telling them there is nothing to export.

**Why this priority**: Called out explicitly as an acceptance criterion ("an export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state — not an empty PDF, not a crash"). It is a correctness guarantee as much as a UX one.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by requesting an export for a period known to contain zero entries and confirming the sheet shows the dedicated empty-period state immediately, with no job ever appearing to run and no file ever offered for download.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user selects a period with zero entries, **When** they request the export, **Then** the sheet shows "Período vazio" ("Nenhum registro nesse período." plus a suggestion to adjust the filter) directly — never "Pendente" or "Processando" first — and offers no download button.
2. **Given** the sheet is showing "Período vazio", **When** the user taps "Fechar", **Then** the sheet dismisses without having created any downloadable file and without affecting My Records' own list or filters.

---

### Edge Cases

- The user taps "Fechar" while the job is still "Pendente" or "Processando": the sheet dismisses and the in-flight job is left alone server-side; the app does not keep polling it in the background once the sheet is gone, and it is not treated as the "current" export if the sheet is reopened.
- The user taps the download icon again while an export sheet/job from a previous tap is still in flight for the same period: this does not create a second concurrent export job — the tap is treated as a no-op (or reopens the same in-flight sheet) rather than firing a second `POST /export/summary`.
- The session expires while the export sheet is open: the existing expired-session overlay (RF07) takes over exactly as it does for the rest of the screen; once re-authenticated, the sheet resumes reflecting the export job's real status rather than being stuck mid-attempt.
- The download itself (PDF or raw data) fails after the job reached a downloadable state (e.g., the signed URL expired or the connection drops mid-download): the corresponding button returns to a retryable state rather than leaving the sheet stuck or silently failing.
- Opening the export sheet, polling its job, or downloading a file does not alter My Records' list, its active filters, its sync badges, or its scroll position in any way.
- Opening My Records itself, its filters, its tags, the chat, the dashboard, or any other screen or action not named in this feature: unaffected by this unit and not touched by it.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: A download icon in My Records' header MUST open the export bottom sheet.

- **FR-007**: When the job fails entirely (no data produced, not only the narrative), the sheet MUST show a failure state with a generic message explaining the export itself could not be generated — text distinct from FR-006's narrative-only explanation, shown the same way regardless of the backend's specific error code — no download control at all, and only the "Fechar" link available (no dedicated in-sheet retry control; retrying means closing the sheet and tapping the download icon again, per FR-011). - **FR-008**: "Baixar PDF" MUST only ever be offered when FR-005's conditions hold, and tapping it MUST download a PDF containing the generated narrative for the exported period.
- **FR-009**: "Baixar dados brutos" MUST be offered in both the FR-005 and FR-006 outcomes, and tapping it MUST download the user's raw entry data for the exported period, independent of whether the narrative ever succeeded.
- **FR-010**: A "Fechar" link MUST be present and functional in every one of the six sheet states ("Pendente", "Processando", "Concluído", "Erro" [FR-006's narrative-only failure], the full-failure state [FR-007], and "Período vazio"), dismissing the sheet without cancelling any in-flight backend job and without affecting My Records' own list, filters, or scroll position.
- **FR-011**: Repeated taps on the download icon, or on a download button that already has a request in flight, MUST NOT create multiple concurrent export jobs or fire duplicate download requests for the same action.
- **FR-012**: If the session expires while the export sheet is open, the existing session-expiration handling (RF07) MUST take over exactly as it does elsewhere on the screen, and the sheet MUST resume reflecting the export job's actual status once re-authenticated rather than remaining stuck.
- **FR-013**: This unit MUST NOT implement manual-tag or category filtering, or any other extension feature (requirements, section 2); MUST NOT implement functionality belonging to units later than RF05 in the build order; and MUST NOT modify the backend, its API contract, or its configuration.

### Key Entities

Produces, at most, two downloadable artifacts (a PDF narrative and the raw data) once it reaches a state where either is available. It is not a journal entry and is never shown anywhere outside the export sheet.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: A user exporting a period that has at least one entry can reach a downloaded, readable narrative PDF end-to-end, with zero crashes and zero empty or malformed files, across all tested periods.
- **SC-002**: In 100% of forced narrative-failure cases (for a period with entries), the user still completes a raw-data download from the same sheet, with a clear explanation of what happened.

- **SC-004**: Closing the export sheet, from any of its five states, leaves My Records' list, active filters, and scroll position completely unchanged in 100% of tested cases.
- **SC-005**: No export attempt — successful, narrative-failed, fully failed, or empty-period — ever leaves the sheet showing a "preparing" or "generating" indicator indefinitely; every attempt reaches one of its defined terminal states within the system's normal response time.

## Assumptions

# Implementation Plan: P-RF05 — Personal summary export

**Branch**: `010-personal-summary-export` (spec directory only — no git branch exists; none of this repo's
extension hooks are configured, per spec.md's own header)

**Date**: 2026-10-24 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/010-personal-summary-export/spec.md`, `docs/input/requirements.md`
§1 (RF05), §6.5 (`export-summary-create`/`export-status-get`/`export-download-get`), §8 (data model
reference), §9 (stack), §13; `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`'s `/export/*` schemas;
`docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md`; `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`;
`docs/input/backend/README.md`'s function-name mapping; `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §2.5; and
`.specify/memory/constitution.md`. Depends on RF07 (`specs/005-multi-source-timeline/`), already implemented —
this is the unit that makes "Meus Registros"' currently-inert download icon
(`records_page.dart`'s `_Header`, comment "no export behavior in this unit") actually work.

## Summary

"Meus Registros"' download icon gains a bottom sheet (`ExportSheet`) that requests an async export job for
whatever period the screen's own active date filter represents (`POST /export/summary`), polls its status
(`GET /export/{jobId}/status`) every 2 seconds, and — once the job reaches a terminal state — offers a PDF
narrative download and/or a raw-data download (`GET /export/{jobId}/download`), each saved/shared via the OS
share sheet. A new feature folder, `lib/features/export/`, is added with its own three-layer structure:
`ExportJob`/`ExportFormat`/`ExportSheetState` (domain, plus a pure `sheetState` derivation of
`export-screen-states.md`'s table), `ExportRepository`/`ExportFileRepository` (domain interfaces),
`ExportRemoteDataSource`/`ExportRepositoryImpl`/`ExportFileRepositoryImpl` (data), and one bloc, `ExportBloc`
(one new instance per sheet open, research.md R6). `core/network/ApiClient` gains one new, export-agnostic
method, `downloadFile()` — a two-step fetch (our backend's 302, then a header-less GET of the signed Storage
URL) that never forwards this app's own credentials to the Storage host (research.md R1). A new dependency,
`share_plus`, provides the "save or share" affordance no existing package in this app covers. The spec's own
resolved Clarification — a sixth, generic failure state distinct from the prototype's one narrative-only
"Erro" — is implemented as a sixth `ExportSheetState`/`ExportState` value, `erroCompleto`/`ExportFailed`
(research.md R4). `records_page.dart`'s `_Header`/`_RecordsPageState` are extended in place to wire the icon
to the sheet, deriving the period from `RecordsBloc`'s existing `DateRangeOption` via RF06's own
`DateRangeBounds` extension (research.md R8) — no new `RecordsBloc` event/state, no new `go_router` route.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Dart 3.13.4 / Flutter 3.47.5 (stable), pinned via `.fvmrc` — unchanged from
F000/RF01/RF03/RF06/RF07.

**Primary Dependencies**: One addition — `share_plus: ^13.3.1` (research.md R2), the OS share sheet for the
two downloadable files this unit produces. Everything else reuses the full existing stack —
`flutter_bloc`, `fpdart`, `get_it`, `equatable`, `dio` (via `ApiClient`, extended with `downloadFile()`),
`path_provider` (already present for the audio pipeline, reused here for a temp file), `go_router` (no new
route); dev-only `mocktail`, `bloc_test`.

**Storage**: None new. `export_jobs`/their downloaded files are explicitly ephemeral (Key Entities: "never
shown anywhere outside the export sheet") — unlike `EntriesLocalCache`/`ChatLocalCache`, this unit adds no
on-device persistence; a downloaded file lives only in the OS temp directory for the lifetime of the share
sheet.

**Testing**: `flutter_test` + `bloc_test` + `mocktail`, unchanged tooling. Coverage via `fvm flutter test
--coverage`, same `lib/**/domain/**` lcov filter (RNF07), now additionally exercising `export_job.dart`'s pure
`sheetState` mapping (R4), `ExportRepositoryImpl`'s silent-refresh-and-retry branches (reused verbatim from
`EntriesRepositoryImpl`'s shape), and `ApiClient.downloadFile()`'s two-leg redirect/fetch logic (a `core/`
addition — `test/core/network/`, mirroring where `sse_frame`/`error_mapper` tests already live).

**Target Platform**: iOS, portrait only — unchanged. No native project file touched beyond whatever
`share_plus`'s own iOS integration requires at the `Info.plist`/Podfile level (its own install instructions;
no custom native code written by this unit).

**Project Type**: Same single Flutter mobile app. One new feature folder, `lib/features/export/`
(domain/data/presentation, Principle V), one cross-cutting `core/network/` addition
(`ApiClient.downloadFile()`), and in-place extensions to `lib/features/records/presentation/pages/
records_page.dart` (`_Header`/`_RecordsPageState`, research.md R8) and `lib/core/di/service_locator.dart`. No
backend/server code, no change to `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`.

**Performance Goals**: RNF01 unchanged. The sheet's "Pendente" state appears synchronously the instant the
download icon is tapped (before the `POST` even resolves), satisfying "a local action is reflected in the UI
in under 100 ms"; the `POST`/polling/download calls themselves are each already covered by the loading-
indicator convention their own sheet states already are (spinner/progress bar), satisfying "any network call
taking longer than 300 ms MUST show a loading indicator" by construction — there is no network call in this
unit's flow that is ever silent.

**Constraints**:
- No manual-tag/category filtering or any other extension feature (FR-013) — the export sheet has no period
  picker, no persona/categorization control of its own.
- No functionality belonging to a unit later than RF05 in the build order (FR-013) — RF09's dashboard
  narrative (`GET /dashboard/narrative`) is a distinct endpoint, never touched here.
- No backend/contract/config change (FR-013) — `downloadFile()`'s two-leg shape and every parsed field name
  (research.md R1/contracts/export-repository.md) are this app's own typed wrapper around what
  `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml` already describes.

  `equatable`/`fpdart`; no `package:flutter`, no `export/data/` class. `ExportBloc` depends only on
  `ExportRepository`/`ExportFileRepository` — never `SessionRepository` directly (research.md R7), never
  `RecordsBloc` (no cross-bloc import).

  `registerFactory`-registered `ExportBloc` (research.md R6) plus a simple tap-guard in
  `_RecordsPageState` (research.md R8/contracts/records-header-export-extension.md) — no second
  `POST /export/summary` can fire for the same tap, and no in-flight job is polled once its sheet is gone.
- Zero visual values hardcoded outside `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` (Principle IV/RNF08) — every new widget
  reuses existing tokens only (data-model.md's widget list) — zero new color/spacing/radius tokens needed,
  since `colorAccent`/`colorSuccess`/`colorError` already exist from F000/RF06/RF07.

**Scale/Scope**: 1 new feature folder (`export/`) with 1 domain entity + 1 pure derivation extension, 2
repository interfaces, 2 data classes + 2 repository impls, 1 bloc (+events/states), 7 new presentation
widgets; 1 extended `core/network/` method (`ApiClient.downloadFile()`); 1 existing `records/` file extended
in place (`records_page.dart`); 1 new dependency (`share_plus`); 5 new DI registrations.

    │   │   └── api_client.dart                           # + downloadFile() (research.md R1)
    │   └── di/
    │       └── service_locator.dart                      # + Export registrations
    └── features/
        ├── export/
        │   ├── domain/
        │   │   ├── entities/
        │   │   │   └── export_job.dart                   # NEW — ExportJobStatus, NarrativeStatus,
        │   │   │                                          #   ExportSheetState, ExportJob, ExportFormat
        │   │   └── repositories/
        │   │       ├── export_repository.dart             # NEW
        │   │       └── export_file_repository.dart         # NEW
        │   ├── data/
        │   │   ├── export_remote_data_source.dart         # NEW
        │   │   ├── export_repository_impl.dart             # NEW
        │   │   └── export_file_repository_impl.dart        # NEW
        │   └── presentation/
        │       ├── bloc/
        │       │   └── export_event.dart / export_state.dart / export_bloc.dart   # NEW
        │       └── widgets/
        │           ├── export_sheet.dart                   # NEW
        │           ├── export_pending_view.dart            # NEW
        │           ├── export_processing_view.dart         # NEW
        │           ├── export_concluded_view.dart          # NEW
        │           ├── export_narrative_failed_view.dart   # NEW
        │           ├── export_failed_view.dart              # NEW
        │           └── export_empty_period_view.dart        # NEW
        └── records/
            └── presentation/
                └── pages/
                    └── records_page.dart                   # extended — _Header/_RecordsPageState wiring
```

**Structure Decision**: One new feature folder, `export/`, following the exact three-layer convention every
prior unit already established — no deviation. The one `core/network/` addition (`ApiClient.downloadFile()`)
lives there rather than inside `export/` because it is not export-specific in shape (any future signed-URL-
download unit reuses it as-is, same reasoning RF04's `sseStream()` was placed in `core/network/` rather than
inside `chat/`). `records/` is extended rather than having the export sheet folded into it because the sheet
is its own independently-testable concern (its own bloc, its own repository boundary) that only happens to be
*opened from* "Meus Registros" — exactly the same "extend the opening screen in place, give the new concern
its own feature folder" shape RF06's `FilterSheet` already established within `records/` itself (the one
difference being `FilterSheet` has no bloc of its own, needing no separate feature folder, while the export
sheet's async job/polling/download concern is large enough to warrant one, mirroring `chat/`'s own
`AppDrawer`-extension-plus-new-feature-folder precedent).

## Complexity Tracking

| Addition | Why Needed | Simpler Alternative Rejected Because |
|---|---|---|
| A second `ApiClient` transport primitive, `downloadFile()` (research.md R1) | `export-download-get` is this app's first endpoint whose success response is a 302-to-a-signed-URL, not JSON — `call()`'s existing `Dio.request<Map<String, dynamic>>()` cannot parse a redirect target's binary bytes, and naively letting `dio` auto-follow the redirect would forward this app's own auth headers to a third-party Storage host | Letting `dio` auto-follow redirects and reusing `call()` as-is — rejected: leaks `apikey`/bearer-token headers to a host they were never scoped for (research.md R1) |
| A new dependency, `share_plus` | This app has no existing mechanism for "hand the user a file to save or share" — `path_provider` alone only produces a path, never a UI affordance to do anything with it | Writing to a permanent path with no share prompt — rejected, a dead end with no in-app file viewer in scope (research.md R2) |
| A sixth `ExportSheetState`/`ExportState` value (`erroCompleto`/`ExportFailed`), beyond the prototype's five named states | The resolved Clarification explicitly requires a failure state "visually and functionally distinct" from the prototype's one narrative-only "Erro" — collapsing both into one state with a flag would directly contradict that resolution | One shared `erro` state with a boolean "is this the narrative-only case" flag — rejected per the Clarification's own explicit wording (research.md R4) |

*No entry needed beyond these three — each is either this unit's first genuinely new mechanism (the
redirect-download transport, the file-share dependency) or a direct, required encoding of spec.md's own
already-resolved Clarification (the sixth state).*

## Post-Design Constitution Check

Re-evaluated after Phase 1 (data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md):

- `export/domain/entities/export_job.dart` and both `export/domain/repositories/*.dart` were re-checked
  against their actual planned imports: `equatable`, `fpdart` (for `Either`/`Unit` signatures), and
  `core/network/failure.dart` only. No `package:flutter`, no `export/data/` class — RNF06/Principle V
  confirmed before any code exists.
- `ExportBloc`'s dependency surface was re-checked: exactly `ExportRepository` + `ExportFileRepository` — no
  `SessionRepository`, no `RecordsBloc` import. Neither `ExportBloc` nor `RecordsBloc` appears in the other's
  planned import list (`no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart` covers this mechanically across `features/` folders).
- Re-checked `ApiClient.downloadFile()`'s exception handling against `call()`'s existing `_mapException` —
  reused verbatim for leg 1; leg 2's storage-host failures fall through the same function's existing no-JSON-
  body branch, so no second, divergent failure-mapping implementation was introduced.
- Re-checked that the second `_dio.request` in `downloadFile()` (the storage leg) sends no
  `apikey`/`Authorization` header at all — confirmed in `contracts/http-client-download-extension.md`'s own
  code listing (Principle III's credential-exposure concern, research.md R1).
- Re-checked that `ExportJob.sheetState`, the one domain helper RNF07 specifically needs to be independently
  testable, has zero constructor dependencies and zero I/O — confirmed pure in data-model.md's own listing.
- Re-checked the `records_page.dart` extension (research.md R8) against Principle V: no new `RecordsEvent`/
  `RecordsState`, no new `go_router` route — `AppRoutes.records` itself is unchanged, and `_Header`'s only
  new dependency is a `VoidCallback` its own parent already owns.
- No change surfaces that touches `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, `.env`, any native iOS project file
  beyond `share_plus`'s own documented install step, or calls an AI provider directly — Principle III remains
  intact. No export code path reaches a manual-tag/category filter or any RF09-owned endpoint — FR-013 holds
  by construction (confirmed by `export/`'s own planned import list containing nothing from
  `features/entries/` tag handling or `dashboard`-shaped calls).

No new violations. Gate remains PASS.

366	  FR-011, FR-012, Edge Cases).

368	---
369	
370	## Dependencies & Execution Order
371	
372	### Phase Dependencies
373	
374	- **Setup (Phase 1)**: No dependencies.
375	- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: Depends on Setup. BLOCKS every user story phase — unlike most features, this
376	  phase contains the entire feature's implementation (T002–T026), because `ExportState`'s sealed-class switch
377	  in `export_sheet.dart` must be exhaustive from first compile.
378	- **User Stories (Phases 3–5)**: All depend on Foundational completion. Each phase's tests are independent of
379	  the others' and can be written/run in any order or in parallel by different people.
380	- **Polish (Phase 6)**: Depends on all three user story phases.
381	
382	### Within Phase 2 (Foundational)
383	
384	T002 → T003 · T004/T005/T006 independent of T002 · T006 → T007 · (T002,T004,T006) → T008 → T009 ·
385	(T004,T008) → T010 → T011 · T005 → T012 → T013 · T014/T015 independent · (T004,T005,T010,T012,T014,T015) →
386	T016 · (T006,T008,T010,T012,T016) → T017 · T018–T023 independent of each other · (T014,T015,T016,T017,
387	T018–T023) → T024 → T025 → T026.
388	
389	### Within Each User Story Phase
390	
391	Bloc test tasks within a phase (T027–T030, T033–T038, T042, T049–T050) share one file
392	(`export_bloc_test.dart`) and are added sequentially, not in parallel, to avoid conflicting edits. Widget test
393	tasks (T031, T039, T040, T043) are each their own file and have no dependency on the bloc test tasks.
394	
395	### Parallel Opportunities
396	
397	- All of T018–T023 (the six state-view widgets) can be built in parallel — six independent files, no
398	  cross-dependency.
399	- T002/T004/T005/T006/T014/T015 (entity, two domain interfaces, `ApiClient` extension, event/state classes)
400	  have no dependency on each other and can start together once Setup is done.
401	- Within each user story phase, the widget test task(s) can run in parallel with that phase's bloc test
402	  tasks, since they touch different files.
403	- The three manual-verification tasks (T032, T041, T044) can be performed by different people once Phase 2's
404	  checkpoint is reached.
405	
406	---
407	
408	## Parallel Example: Phase 2 widget layer
409	
410	```bash
411	Task: "Create export_pending_view.dart"
412	Task: "Create export_processing_view.dart"
413	Task: "Create export_concluded_view.dart"
414	Task: "Create export_narrative_failed_view.dart"
415	Task: "Create export_failed_view.dart"
416	Task: "Create export_empty_period_view.dart"
417	# All six (T018–T023) are independent files — only export_sheet.dart (T024) needs all six done first.
418	```
419	
420	---
421	
422	## Implementation Strategy
423	
424	### MVP scope
425	
426	Because spec.md assigns **P1 to both User Story 1 and User Story 2** (US2 is called out explicitly as its own
427	acceptance criterion, not a nice-to-have), the smallest responsible MVP is **Phase 1 + Phase 2 + Phase 3 (US1)
428	+ Phase 4 (US2)** — a narrative-failure falling back to raw data is as core to RF05's trust story as the PDF
429	path itself. User Story 3 (empty-period handling, P2) is the first increment after that.
430	
431	### Incremental delivery
432	
433	1. Setup + Foundational (Phases 1–2) → the full feature compiles, is wired into "Meus Registros", passes its
434	   own tests.
435	2. Add US1's tests + manual pass (Phase 3) → confident in the narrative-PDF happy path. **MVP checkpoint 1.**
436	3. Add US2's tests + manual pass (Phase 4) → confident the AI narrative can never block the user's own data.
437	   **Full MVP.**
438	4. Add US3's tests + manual pass (Phase 5) → confident the empty-period edge case never shows a spinner.
439	5. Polish (Phase 6) → `flutter analyze`, architecture tests, RNF07 coverage gate, remaining edge cases.
440	
441	### Parallel team strategy
442	
443	With multiple people: one completes Setup + Foundational alone (it's one tightly-coupled unit, hard to split
444	usefully). Once Phase 2's checkpoint is reached, up to three people can each own one user story phase's
445	tests + manual verification in parallel — none of Phases 3–5 touch each other's test files except the shared
446	`export_bloc_test.dart` (coordinate on that one file, or have one person own all bloc-test additions).
447

# Tasks: P-RF05 — Personal summary export

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/010-personal-summary-export/`
**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md (all present)

**Tests**: Included. RNF07 (≥80% domain coverage) and RNF09 (Either + full error-scenario coverage) are
gates this plan explicitly carries into tasks, and every contract in `contracts/` enumerates its own numbered
test-scenario table — these are treated as required deliverables, not optional extras.

**Organization**: `ExportState` is a single Dart `sealed class` with six variants, and the one widget that
renders it (`export_sheet.dart`) must switch over all six exhaustively from the moment it compiles — so the
full domain/data/bloc/widget implementation is **one indivisible unit** (Phase 2, Foundational) rather than
something that can be built one user story at a time. Each user story phase (3–5) instead adds the
**automated tests and manual verification that specifically prove that story's acceptance scenarios**,
independently of the other stories' tests — this is this feature's actual "independently testable" seam,
given its architecture.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependency on an incomplete task)
- **[Story]**: US1 / US2 / US3, per spec.md's priorities (US1 and US2 are both P1; US3 is P2)

## Path Conventions

Single Flutter app. `lib/features/export/` (new, 3-layer), `lib/core/network/api_client.dart` (extended),
`lib/core/di/service_locator.dart` (extended), `lib/features/records/presentation/pages/records_page.dart`
(extended). Tests mirror `lib/` under `test/`, matching this repo's existing `entries/`/`chat`/`records`
layout.

---

## Phase 1: Setup

- [X] T001 Add `share_plus: ^13.3.1` to `pubspec.yaml`'s dependencies (research.md R2) and run
  `fvm flutter pub get` — `path_provider: ^2.1.5` is already present, no other dependency change.

---

## Phase 2: Foundational (Blocking Prerequisites)

**Purpose**: The complete `export/` feature (domain → data → bloc → widgets) plus the two cross-cutting
extensions (`ApiClient.downloadFile()`, `records_page.dart`'s icon wiring) that every user story depends on.
No user story's acceptance scenario is observable, through the UI or a bloc test, until this phase is done.

### Domain layer

- [X] T002 [P] Create `ExportJobStatus` (`pending`/`processing`/`dataReady`/`done`/`error`), `NarrativeStatus`
  (`pending`/`processing`/`done`/`failed`/`skipped`) and `ExportSheetState`
  (`pendente`/`processando`/`concluido`/`erroNarrativa`/`erroCompleto`/`periodoVazio`) enums; the `ExportJob`
  `Equatable` entity (`jobId` `String`, `status` `ExportJobStatus`, `narrativeStatus` `NarrativeStatus`,
  `entryCount` `int?`, `errorCode` `String?`, `narrativeErrorCode` `String?`, `downloadAvailable` `bool`); and
  the pure `ExportJobSheetState.sheetState` extension implementing `export-screen-states.md`'s table verbatim
  (`pending`→`pendente`; `processing`→`processando`; `dataReady`→`processando` regardless of
  `narrativeStatus`; `done`+`done`→`concluido`; `done`+(`failed`|`skipped`)→`erroNarrativa`; `error`→
  `erroCompleto`) in `lib/features/export/domain/entities/export_job.dart` (data-model.md, research.md R4).
- [X] T003 [P] Write unit tests covering `ExportJob.sheetState`'s full 6-row mapping as a total, pure
  function (zero constructor dependencies, zero I/O) in
  `test/features/export/domain/entities/export_job_test.dart` (research.md R4, RNF07).
- [X] T004 [P] Create the `ExportFormat` enum (`pdf`, `raw`) and the `ExportRepository` abstract interface —
  `Future<Either<Failure, String>> create({required DateTime? periodStart, required DateTime? periodEnd})`,
  `Future<Either<Failure, ExportJob>> status(String jobId)`,
  `Future<Either<Failure, Uint8List>> download({required String jobId, required ExportFormat format})` — in
  `lib/features/export/domain/repositories/export_repository.dart` (contracts/export-repository.md).
- [X] T005 [P] Create the `ExportFileRepository` abstract interface —
  `Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> share({required Uint8List bytes, required ExportFormat format})` — in
  `lib/features/export/domain/repositories/export_file_repository.dart` (contracts/export-repository.md).

### Core network

- [X] T006 [P] Add `Future<Either<Failure, Uint8List>> downloadFile(String function, {List<String>?
  pathSegments, Map<String, dynamic>? queryParameters, AuthMode authMode = AuthMode.userSession})` to
  `lib/core/network/api_client.dart` (`call()`/`sseStream()` unchanged): leg 1 is a `GET` to `function` with
  `followRedirects: false` and `validateStatus: (status) => status != null && status < 400`, sending the same
  `apikey`/`Authorization` headers `call()` already sends; a non-`302` status or a missing `location` header
  returns `Left(ValidationFailure(message: 'Malformed response: expected a 302 redirect', requestId: ''))`;
  leg 2 is a header-less `GET` of the `location` URL with `responseType: ResponseType.bytes`, returning
  `Right(Uint8List.fromList(...))` on success; both legs' `DioException`s map through the existing
  `_mapException` (contracts/http-client-download-extension.md, research.md R1).
- [X] T007 [P] Write tests for `ApiClient.downloadFile()`'s 7 contract scenarios — 302+bytes success;
  leg-1 `200` (no redirect) → `ValidationFailure`; `302` with no `location` header → `ValidationFailure`;
  leg-1 `DioException` with `{code: 'AUTH_EXPIRED'}` → `AuthExpiredFailure`; leg-2 `connectionTimeout` →
  `NetworkTimeoutFailure`; leg-2 exception with no `response` at all → `NetworkOfflineFailure`; `queryParameters:
  {'format': 'raw'}` reaches leg 1's URL verbatim — in `test/core/network/api_client_download_test.dart`
  (contracts/http-client-download-extension.md).

### Data layer

- [X] T008 Create `ExportRemoteDataSource` in `lib/features/export/data/export_remote_data_source.dart`,
  calling `ApiClient.call('export-summary-create', method: 'POST', body: {periodStart, periodEnd,
  includeNarrative: true})` and parsing `data.jobId`; calling `ApiClient.call('export-status-get', method:
  'GET', pathSegments: [jobId])` and parsing the full `ExportJob` (`status`'s wire value `data_ready` parses
  to `ExportJobStatus.dataReady` via an explicit lookup table, not `.byName`; every other enum value parses via
  `.byName`); delegating `download` to `ApiClient.downloadFile('export-download-get', pathSegments: [jobId],
  queryParameters: {'format': format.name})` unparsed (depends on T002, T004, T006) (data-model.md,
  contracts/export-repository.md).
- [X] T009 [P] Write unit tests for `ExportRemoteDataSource`'s three parse paths, including the `data_ready`
  lookup-table case, in `test/features/export/data/export_remote_data_source_test.dart` (depends on T008).
- [X] T010 Create `ExportRepositoryImpl` in `lib/features/export/data/export_repository_impl.dart`,
  implementing `create`/`status`/`download` via `ExportRemoteDataSource`, each wrapped in the
  `_retryAfterSilentRefresh` shape copied verbatim from `EntriesRepositoryImpl` (exactly one retry via
  `SessionRepository.refresh()` on a first-attempt `AuthExpiredFailure`; a second `AuthExpiredFailure` after
  that retry is returned as-is, no loop); `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` (400) maps through the existing, shared
  `ErrorMapper.fromResponse` to `Left(ExportEmptyPeriodFailure)` — already defined in
  `lib/core/network/failure.dart` (depends on T004, T008) (contracts/export-repository.md, research.md R7).
- [X] T011 [P] Write tests for `ExportRepositoryImpl`'s 10 contract scenarios — `create()` success /
  `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` / timeout / malformed body / no-connection; `status()` `data_ready`+`processing` parse /
  malformed body; silent-refresh retry success / retry-also-fails (exactly one retry, no loop); `download()`
  bytes passthrough — in `test/features/export/data/export_repository_impl_test.dart` (depends on T010).
- [X] T012 [P] Create `ExportFileRepositoryImpl.share` in
  `lib/features/export/data/export_file_repository_impl.dart`: writes `bytes` to
  `(await getTemporaryDirectory()).path` as `cerne-resumo.pdf` (`ExportFormat.pdf`) or `cerne-dados.json`
  (`ExportFormat.raw`), then calls `Share.shareXFiles([XFile(file.path)])`; any write/share exception maps to
  `Left(NetworkTimeoutFailure(message: 'Falha ao salvar/compartilhar o arquivo.', requestId: ''))`; a
  user-cancelled share (a non-throwing `ShareResult` from `share_plus`) is treated as `Right(unit)` (depends on
  T005) (contracts/export-repository.md, research.md R2).
- [X] T013 [P] Write tests for `ExportFileRepositoryImpl.share`'s 2 contract scenarios — write+share success
  including a user-cancelled share resolving to `Right(unit)`; a file-write throw resolving to
  `Left(NetworkTimeoutFailure)` — in `test/features/export/data/export_file_repository_impl_test.dart`
  (depends on T012).

### Presentation — bloc

- [X] T014 [P] Create the `ExportEvent` sealed classes — `ExportRequested(DateTime? periodStart, DateTime?
  periodEnd)`, `ExportStatusPollTicked`, `PdfDownloadRequested`, `RawDataDownloadRequested` — in
  `lib/features/export/presentation/bloc/export_event.dart` (data-model.md).
- [X] T015 [P] Create the `ExportState` sealed classes — `ExportPending`, `ExportProcessing`,
  `ExportConcluded({required jobId, isDownloadingPdf = false, isDownloadingRaw = false, pdfDownloadFailure,
  rawDownloadFailure})`, `ExportNarrativeFailed({required jobId, isDownloadingRaw = false,
  rawDownloadFailure})`, `ExportFailed`, `ExportEmptyPeriod` — in
  `lib/features/export/presentation/bloc/export_state.dart` (data-model.md).
- [X] T016 Create `ExportBloc extends Bloc<ExportEvent, ExportState>` (constructor takes `ExportRepository` +
  `ExportFileRepository` only — never `SessionRepository`, never any `RecordsBloc` type) in
  `lib/features/export/presentation/bloc/export_bloc.dart`, implementing contracts/export-bloc.md's full
  event→state sequence: `_onExportRequested` emits `ExportPending()`, calls `exportRepository.create(...)` —
  `ExportEmptyPeriodFailure` → emit `ExportEmptyPeriod()` (terminal); `AuthExpiredFailure` → fire
  `reauthRequired`, emit `ExportFailed()` (terminal); any other `Failure` → emit `ExportFailed()` (terminal);
  success → store `_jobId`, `add(const ExportStatusPollTicked())`. `_onStatusPollTicked` calls
  `exportRepository.status(_jobId!)` — on failure, fire `reauthRequired` if `AuthExpiredFailure`, leave state
  unchanged, re-arm `Timer(const Duration(seconds: 2), () => add(const ExportStatusPollTicked()))`; on success,
  map `job.sheetState` to `ExportPending`/`ExportProcessing` (re-arm timer, not terminal) or

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Setup (Phase 1)**: No dependencies.
- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: Depends on Setup. BLOCKS every user story phase — unlike most features, this
  phase contains the entire feature's implementation (T002–T026), because `ExportState`'s sealed-class switch
  in `export_sheet.dart` must be exhaustive from first compile.
- **User Stories (Phases 3–5)**: All depend on Foundational completion. Each phase's tests are independent of
  the others' and can be written/run in any order or in parallel by different people.
- **Polish (Phase 6)**: Depends on all three user story phases.

### Within Phase 2 (Foundational)

T002 → T003 · T004/T005/T006 independent of T002 · T006 → T007 · (T002,T004,T006) → T008 → T009 ·
(T004,T008) → T010 → T011 · T005 → T012 → T013 · T014/T015 independent · (T004,T005,T010,T012,T014,T015) →
T016 · (T006,T008,T010,T012,T016) → T017 · T018–T023 independent of each other · (T014,T015,T016,T017,
T018–T023) → T024 → T025 → T026.

### Within Each User Story Phase

Bloc test tasks within a phase (T027–T030, T033–T038, T042, T049–T050) share one file
(`export_bloc_test.dart`) and are added sequentially, not in parallel, to avoid conflicting edits. Widget test
tasks (T031, T039, T040, T043) are each their own file and have no dependency on the bloc test tasks.

### Parallel Opportunities

- All of T018–T023 (the six state-view widgets) can be built in parallel — six independent files, no
  cross-dependency.
- T002/T004/T005/T006/T014/T015 (entity, two domain interfaces, `ApiClient` extension, event/state classes)
  have no dependency on each other and can start together once Setup is done.
- Within each user story phase, the widget test task(s) can run in parallel with that phase's bloc test
  tasks, since they touch different files.
- The three manual-verification tasks (T032, T041, T044) can be performed by different people once Phase 2's
  checkpoint is reached.

## Implementation Strategy

### MVP scope

Because spec.md assigns **P1 to both User Story 1 and User Story 2** (US2 is called out explicitly as its own
acceptance criterion, not a nice-to-have), the smallest responsible MVP is **Phase 1 + Phase 2 + Phase 3 (US1)
+ Phase 4 (US2)** — a narrative-failure falling back to raw data is as core to RF05's trust story as the PDF
path itself. User Story 3 (empty-period handling, P2) is the first increment after that.

### Incremental delivery

1. Setup + Foundational (Phases 1–2) → the full feature compiles, is wired into "Meus Registros", passes its
   own tests.
2. Add US1's tests + manual pass (Phase 3) → confident in the narrative-PDF happy path. **MVP checkpoint 1.**
3. Add US2's tests + manual pass (Phase 4) → confident the AI narrative can never block the user's own data.
   **Full MVP.**
4. Add US3's tests + manual pass (Phase 5) → confident the empty-period edge case never shows a spinner.
5. Polish (Phase 6) → `flutter analyze`, architecture tests, RNF07 coverage gate, remaining edge cases.

### Parallel team strategy

With multiple people: one completes Setup + Foundational alone (it's one tightly-coupled unit, hard to split
usefully). Once Phase 2's checkpoint is reached, up to three people can each own one user story phase's
tests + manual verification in parallel — none of Phases 3–5 touch each other's test files except the shared
`export_bloc_test.dart` (coordinate on that one file, or have one person own all bloc-test additions).

24	# Cerne Constitution
25	
26	## Core Principles
27	
28	### I. Product Source of Truth
29	`docs/input/` — `requirements.md`, `prototype/`, and `backend/` — is the
30	authoritative source for product behavior. `requirements.md` defines
31	functional and quality requirements, screens, the API surface, delivery
32	order, and technical constraints; `prototype/` is the frozen visual
33	reference and its token/state extract; `backend/` documents the existing
34	API, error taxonomy, screen-state map, sync-badge semantics, and fixtures.
35	Where these documents are silent, implementers MUST make a reasonable
36	technical decision rather than block on clarification. Files under
37	`docs/input/` are frozen inputs and MUST NOT be edited by anyone working in
38	this repository.
39	
40	Rationale: a reflective-journaling app with a frozen, already-documented
41	backend has exactly one place where ambiguity should be resolved — the
42	product input — so decisions stay traceable and the backend contract stays
43	stable.
44	
45	### II. Fixed Technology Stack
46	The app is built with Flutter and Dart at the version pinned via `fvm`,
47	using `flutter_bloc` for state management and Clean Architecture with three
48	layers per feature. Error handling MUST use `fpdart`, with every repository
49	returning `Either<Failure, T>`. Test doubles MUST use `mocktail`. Speech-to-
50	text runs on-device via `whisper_ggml`; audio content MUST NEVER be sent to
51	the backend. The shipping platform is iOS. Choices not fixed here — routing,
52	HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics,
53	and charting — are open implementation decisions.
54	
55	Rationale: a single, non-negotiable stack removes a whole category of
56	architectural debate and keeps the codebase consistent across features
57	built by different contributors or at different times.
58	
59	### III. Backend Boundary — Frozen Backend, No Direct AI Calls
60	The backend is already built and frozen. The app consumes it strictly as
61	documented in `docs/input/backend/`, including its API contract
62	(`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`); the app MUST NOT change the
63	backend, its API contract, or its configuration. All AI features, including
64	semantic search, are provided exclusively by the backend — the app MUST
65	NEVER call an AI provider directly. Configuration and credentials come from
66	a project-root `.env` with exactly two variables: `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` and
67	`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`. Every call to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>` MUST
68	carry the header `apikey: <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>`. The `Authorization: Bearer`
69	header carries `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` for operations that need no user session
70	(sign-up, login, refresh) and the user's access token for every operation
71	marked `bearerAuth` in the OpenAPI contract. `.env` and any credential MUST
72	NEVER be committed.
73	
74	Rationale: the backend and its AI integrations are out of this project's
75	scope and already relied upon elsewhere; treating them as an immutable,
76	narrowly-accessed contract prevents scope creep and accidental coupling or
77	credential leakage.
78	
79	### IV. Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity
80	`lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography,
81	spacing, and radii. No visual value MAY be hardcoded anywhere else. The UI
82	MUST be faithful to `docs/input/prototype/`. UI text MUST be in Portuguese,
83	exactly as written in the prototype; code identifiers, comments, and project
84	documentation MUST be in English.
85	
86	Rationale: a single token source makes visual fidelity (RNF08) mechanically
87	checkable, and separating UI language (Portuguese, matching the frozen
88	prototype) from code language (English) keeps the codebase reviewable while
89	preserving the product's voice.
90	
91	### V. Clean Architecture Folder Convention
92	Code MUST follow the folder convention:
93	```
94	lib/
95	  core/
96	  features/
97	    <feature>/
98	      data/
99	      domain/
100	      presentation/
101	```
102	The domain layer MUST comply with RNF06: zero layer violations — it MUST
103	NOT import `package:flutter` nor any class from a feature's `data/` layer.
104	
105	Rationale: a fixed, enforced folder shape and a flutter/data-free domain
106	layer make the domain independently testable and keep business rules
107	portable regardless of UI or persistence choices.
108	
109	## Quality Standards (RNF01–RNF09)
110	
111	These targets from `docs/input/requirements.md` are binding quality gates:
112	
113	- **RNF01 — Interaction latency**: a local action MUST be reflected in the

<!--

Version change: (unratified template) → 1.0.0
Rationale: Initial ratification. The prior file on disk still contained only
unfilled template placeholders ([PROJECT_NAME], [PRINCIPLE_1_NAME], ...) and
never expressed concrete governance, so this is treated as the first adopted
version rather than an amendment.
Modified principles: n/a (no prior concrete principles existed)
Added sections:
  - Core Principles I–V (Product Source of Truth; Fixed Technology Stack;
    Backend Boundary — Frozen Backend, No Direct AI Calls; Design Token
    Discipline & Visual Fidelity; Clean Architecture Folder Convention)
  - Quality Standards (RNF01–RNF09)
  - Scope & Delivery Boundaries
  - Governance
Removed sections: none
Deferred placeholders / TODOs: none — all fields resolved from user-supplied
principles and docs/input/requirements.md.
Templates reviewed for alignment: not modified by this command (out of scope
per the constitution command's scope guard); plan/spec/tasks templates should
be checked against Principles II, III and V on their next edit.
-->

# Cerne Constitution

## Core Principles

### I. Product Source of Truth
`docs/input/` — `requirements.md`, `prototype/`, and `backend/` — is the
authoritative source for product behavior. `requirements.md` defines
functional and quality requirements, screens, the API surface, delivery
order, and technical constraints; `prototype/` is the frozen visual
reference and its token/state extract; `backend/` documents the existing
API, error taxonomy, screen-state map, sync-badge semantics, and fixtures.
Where these documents are silent, implementers MUST make a reasonable
technical decision rather than block on clarification. Files under
`docs/input/` are frozen inputs and MUST NOT be edited by anyone working in
this repository.

Rationale: a reflective-journaling app with a frozen, already-documented
backend has exactly one place where ambiguity should be resolved — the
product input — so decisions stay traceable and the backend contract stays
stable.

### II. Fixed Technology Stack
The app is built with Flutter and Dart at the version pinned via `fvm`,
using `flutter_bloc` for state management and Clean Architecture with three
layers per feature. Error handling MUST use `fpdart`, with every repository
returning `Either<Failure, T>`. Test doubles MUST use `mocktail`. Speech-to-
text runs on-device via `whisper_ggml`; audio content MUST NEVER be sent to
the backend. The shipping platform is iOS. Choices not fixed here — routing,
HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics,
and charting — are open implementation decisions.

Rationale: a single, non-negotiable stack removes a whole category of
architectural debate and keeps the codebase consistent across features
built by different contributors or at different times.

### III. Backend Boundary — Frozen Backend, No Direct AI Calls
The backend is already built and frozen. The app consumes it strictly as
documented in `docs/input/backend/`, including its API contract
(`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`); the app MUST NOT change the
backend, its API contract, or its configuration. All AI features, including
semantic search, are provided exclusively by the backend — the app MUST
NEVER call an AI provider directly. Configuration and credentials come from
a project-root `.env` with exactly two variables: `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` and
`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`. Every call to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>` MUST
carry the header `apikey: <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>`. The `Authorization: Bearer`
header carries `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` for operations that need no user session
(sign-up, login, refresh) and the user's access token for every operation
marked `bearerAuth` in the OpenAPI contract. `.env` and any credential MUST
NEVER be committed.

Rationale: the backend and its AI integrations are out of this project's
scope and already relied upon elsewhere; treating them as an immutable,
narrowly-accessed contract prevents scope creep and accidental coupling or
credential leakage.

### IV. Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity
`lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography,
spacing, and radii. No visual value MAY be hardcoded anywhere else. The UI
MUST be faithful to `docs/input/prototype/`. UI text MUST be in Portuguese,
exactly as written in the prototype; code identifiers, comments, and project
documentation MUST be in English.

Rationale: a single token source makes visual fidelity (RNF08) mechanically
checkable, and separating UI language (Portuguese, matching the frozen
prototype) from code language (English) keeps the codebase reviewable while
preserving the product's voice.

### V. Clean Architecture Folder Convention
Code MUST follow the folder convention:
```
lib/
  core/
  features/
    <feature>/
      data/
      domain/
      presentation/
```
The domain layer MUST comply with RNF06: zero layer violations — it MUST
NOT import `package:flutter` nor any class from a feature's `data/` layer.

Rationale: a fixed, enforced folder shape and a flutter/data-free domain
layer make the domain independently testable and keep business rules
portable regardless of UI or persistence choices.

## Quality Standards (RNF01–RNF09)

These targets from `docs/input/requirements.md` are binding quality gates:

- **RNF01 — Interaction latency**: a local action MUST be reflected in the
  UI in under 100 ms; any network call taking longer than 300 ms MUST show a
  loading indicator.
- **RNF02 — PII stripping**: performed backend-side via Claude Haiku 4.5
  with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model; the app
  implements no PII-detection logic of its own.
- **RNF03 — Zero data retention**: a backend-side policy; the app MUST NOT
  introduce its own retention beyond what the backend requires.
- **RNF04 — Row Level Security (RLS)**: enforced backend-side; the app MUST
  assume RLS is authoritative and MUST NEVER attempt to bypass it.
- **RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD)**: the app MUST expose
  the account-deletion flow (`DELETE /account`) from Settings.
- **RNF06 — Zero layer violations**: see Principle V; 0 violations is the
  target.
- **RNF07 — Domain test coverage**: `lib/**/domain/**` MUST reach at least
  80% test coverage.
- **RNF08 — Visual fidelity**: every screen MUST match the prototype's
  color, typography, and spacing, with 0 hardcoded visual values outside
  `design_tokens.dart`.
- **RNF09 — Consistent network-error handling**: every repository MUST use
  the `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart`; every write endpoint (5
  endpoints) MUST handle timeout, malformed response, and no-connection
  failures, each covered by `mocktail` tests (15 of 15 scenarios).

## Scope & Delivery Boundaries

- Functional requirements MUST be implemented in the delivery order given in
  `docs/input/requirements.md`.
- Extension features (section 2 of `requirements.md`) are explicitly out of
  scope and MUST NOT be implemented beyond an optional placeholder menu
  entry.
- The following actions are prohibited in this repository:
  - Changing the backend, its API contract, or its configuration.
  - Calling AI providers directly from the app.
  - Writing visual values (colors, font sizes, spacing, radii) outside
    `design_tokens.dart`.
  - Implementing extension features.
  - Committing `.env` or any credential.
  - Editing files under `docs/input/`.

## Governance

This constitution supersedes any conflicting practice, template, or
instruction used in this repository. Every plan, spec, task list, and
review MUST verify compliance with these principles before work is
considered done; any deviation MUST be justified in writing in the relevant
artifact (plan or PR description) or the work MUST be rejected.

**Amendment procedure**: amendments are proposed by editing this file,
describing the change and rationale, and are adopted once the project owner
accepts the change (commit to this file constitutes adoption in this
single-maintainer project). Each amendment MUST update the Sync Impact
Report at the top of this file and the version/date line below.

**Versioning policy** (semantic versioning for this document):
- **MAJOR** — backward-incompatible governance or principle removal/
  redefinition.
- **MINOR** — a new principle or section added, or materially expanded
  guidance.
- **PATCH** — wording clarifications, typo fixes, non-semantic refinements.

**Compliance review**: any change to `lib/` MUST be checked against the
Core Principles and Quality Standards above before merge; violations of
RNF06–RNF09 in particular are release blockers.

**Version**: 1.0.0 | **Ratified**: 2026-10-11 | **Last Amended**: 2026-10-11

content.content:
1	# Contract: `ExportBloc`
2	
3	`lib/features/export/presentation/bloc/export_bloc.dart` (+ `export_event.dart`/`export_state.dart`). One new
4	instance per `showModalBottomSheet` call (`registerFactory`, research.md R6) — never reused across sheet
5	opens.
6	
7	```dart
8	class ExportBloc extends Bloc<ExportEvent, ExportState> {
9	  ExportBloc({required ExportRepository exportRepository, required ExportFileRepository exportFileRepository});
10	
11	  Stream<void> get reauthRequired;   // one-shot, identical shape to RecordsBloc's (research.md R7)
12	}
13	```
14	
15	Depends only on `ExportRepository`/`ExportFileRepository` — never `SessionRepository`, never `RecordsBloc` or
16	any of its event/state types.
17	
18	## Event → state sequence
19	
20	```
21	ExportRequested(periodStart, periodEnd)
22	  -> emit ExportPending()
23	  -> ExportRepository.create(periodStart, periodEnd)
24	     -> Left(ExportEmptyPeriodFailure)         -> emit ExportEmptyPeriod()                      [terminal]
25	     -> Left(AuthExpiredFailure)               -> reauthRequired.add(null); emit ExportFailed()  [terminal]
26	     -> Left(other Failure)                    -> emit ExportFailed()                            [terminal]
27	     -> Right(jobId)                           -> store _jobId; add(ExportStatusPollTicked())
28	
29	ExportStatusPollTicked
30	  -> ExportRepository.status(_jobId!)
31	     -> Left(AuthExpiredFailure)  -> reauthRequired.add(null); re-arm Timer(2s, add(ExportStatusPollTicked()))
32	     -> Left(other Failure)       -> re-arm Timer(2s, add(ExportStatusPollTicked())); state unchanged
33	     -> Right(job) where job.sheetState is:
34	        pendente     -> emit ExportPending();     re-arm Timer(2s, ...)
35	        processando   -> emit ExportProcessing();  re-arm Timer(2s, ...)
36	        concluido     -> emit ExportConcluded(jobId: job.jobId)                                  [terminal]
37	        erroNarrativa -> emit ExportNarrativeFailed(jobId: job.jobId)                            [terminal]
38	        erroCompleto  -> emit ExportFailed()                                                     [terminal]
39	
40	PdfDownloadRequested                             (ExportConcluded only)
41	  -> no-op if state.isDownloadingPdf

# Contract: `ExportBloc`

`lib/features/export/presentation/bloc/export_bloc.dart` (+ `export_event.dart`/`export_state.dart`). One new
instance per `showModalBottomSheet` call (`registerFactory`, research.md R6) — never reused across sheet
opens.

```dart
class ExportBloc extends Bloc<ExportEvent, ExportState> {
  ExportBloc({required ExportRepository exportRepository, required ExportFileRepository exportFileRepository});

  Stream<void> get reauthRequired;   // one-shot, identical shape to RecordsBloc's (research.md R7)
}
```

Depends only on `ExportRepository`/`ExportFileRepository` — never `SessionRepository`, never `RecordsBloc` or
any of its event/state types.

## Event → state sequence

```
ExportRequested(periodStart, periodEnd)
  -> emit ExportPending()
  -> ExportRepository.create(periodStart, periodEnd)
     -> Left(ExportEmptyPeriodFailure)         -> emit ExportEmptyPeriod()                      [terminal]
     -> Left(AuthExpiredFailure)               -> reauthRequired.add(null); emit ExportFailed()  [terminal]
     -> Left(other Failure)                    -> emit ExportFailed()                            [terminal]
     -> Right(jobId)                           -> store _jobId; add(ExportStatusPollTicked())

ExportStatusPollTicked
  -> ExportRepository.status(_jobId!)
     -> Left(AuthExpiredFailure)  -> reauthRequired.add(null); re-arm Timer(2s, add(ExportStatusPollTicked()))
     -> Left(other Failure)       -> re-arm Timer(2s, add(ExportStatusPollTicked())); state unchanged
     -> Right(job) where job.sheetState is:
        pendente     -> emit ExportPending();     re-arm Timer(2s, ...)
        processando   -> emit ExportProcessing();  re-arm Timer(2s, ...)
        concluido     -> emit ExportConcluded(jobId: job.jobId)                                  [terminal]
        erroNarrativa -> emit ExportNarrativeFailed(jobId: job.jobId)                            [terminal]
        erroCompleto  -> emit ExportFailed()                                                     [terminal]

PdfDownloadRequested                             (ExportConcluded only)
  -> no-op if state.isDownloadingPdf
  -> emit state.copyWith(isDownloadingPdf: true, pdfDownloadFailure: null)
  -> ExportRepository.download(jobId, ExportFormat.pdf)
     -> Left(failure) -> (reauthRequired if AuthExpiredFailure) emit state.copyWith(isDownloadingPdf: false, pdfDownloadFailure: failure)
     -> Right(bytes)  -> ExportFileRepository.share(bytes, ExportFormat.pdf)
        -> Left(failure) -> emit state.copyWith(isDownloadingPdf: false, pdfDownloadFailure: failure)
        -> Right(_)      -> emit state.copyWith(isDownloadingPdf: false, pdfDownloadFailure: null)

RawDataDownloadRequested                          (ExportConcluded or ExportNarrativeFailed)
  -> identical shape to PdfDownloadRequested, targeting ExportFormat.raw / isDownloadingRaw / rawDownloadFailure
```

- "Terminal" means `_pollTimer` is **not** re-armed — no further `ExportStatusPollTicked` is ever dispatched
  for that `ExportBloc` instance after reaching one of `ExportConcluded`/`ExportNarrativeFailed`/
  `ExportFailed`/`ExportEmptyPeriod` (SC-005).
- A poll-call failure (any cause, including a non-recoverable `AuthExpiredFailure`) never itself transitions
  the sheet to `ExportFailed` — only a job whose own `status` the backend reports as `error` does (research.md
  R4/R7). This is deliberate: a transient network hiccup mid-poll must not be indistinguishable from the
  job itself having failed.
- `close()` cancels `_pollTimer` and closes `_reauthController` — mirrors `RecordsBloc.close()` exactly.

## Test scenarios this contract owns

| # | Scenario | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ExportRequested` where `create()` succeeds | states emitted, in order: `ExportPending()`, then (after the first poll) whatever `status()`'s first response maps to |
| 2 | `ExportRequested` where `create()` returns `ExportEmptyPeriodFailure` | states: `ExportPending()`, `ExportEmptyPeriod()` — no poll ever dispatched |
| 3 | `ExportRequested` where `create()` returns `NetworkOfflineFailure` | states: `ExportPending()`, `ExportFailed()` — no poll ever dispatched |
| 4 | `ExportRequested` where `create()` returns `AuthExpiredFailure` (post-retry) | states: `ExportPending()`, `ExportFailed()`; `reauthRequired` emits exactly once |
| 5 | Poll sequence: `pending` → `processing` → `done`/`done` | states: `ExportPending()`, `ExportProcessing()`, `ExportConcluded(jobId)` — exactly 3 terminal-bound emissions, `_pollTimer` armed twice, never a third time |
| 6 | Poll sequence: `processing` → `done`/`failed` | states end on `ExportNarrativeFailed(jobId)` |
| 7 | Poll sequence: `processing` → `error` | states end on `ExportFailed()` |
| 8 | One poll tick fails with `NetworkTimeoutFailure`, the next succeeds and reaches `done`/`done` | the failed tick produces **no** state emission at all; the sheet never flashes `ExportFailed()` for a transient poll failure |
| 9 | `PdfDownloadRequested` dispatched twice in a row before the first resolves | `ExportRepository.download` is called exactly once (the second dispatch is a no-op per `isDownloadingPdf`) |
| 10 | `PdfDownloadRequested` where `download()` succeeds but `share()` fails | final state: `ExportConcluded(isDownloadingPdf: false, pdfDownloadFailure: <failure>)` — `jobId` unchanged, `rawDownloadFailure` untouched |
| 11 | `RawDataDownloadRequested` from `ExportNarrativeFailed` succeeds | final state: `ExportNarrativeFailed(isDownloadingRaw: false, rawDownloadFailure: null)` — never transitions to `ExportConcluded` |
| 12 | `RawDataDownloadRequested` dispatched twice in a row before the first resolves (from either `ExportConcluded` or `ExportNarrativeFailed`) | `ExportRepository.download` is called exactly once (the second dispatch is a no-op per `isDownloadingRaw`) |
| 13 | `RawDataDownloadRequested` from `ExportNarrativeFailed` where `download()` succeeds but `share()` fails | final state: `ExportNarrativeFailed(isDownloadingRaw: false, rawDownloadFailure: <failure>)` — `jobId` unchanged |

3	Extends `_Header`/`_RecordsPageState` in place (FR-001/FR-002/FR-011). `RecordsBloc`/`RecordsEvent`/
4	`RecordsState` are unchanged — no new event, no new field (research.md R8).
5	
6	```dart
7	class _Header extends StatelessWidget {
8	  const _Header({required this.onExportPressed});
9	  final VoidCallback onExportPressed;
10	
11	  @override
12	  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
13	    return Padding(
14	      // ...unchanged back-arrow + title...
15	      child: Row(
16	        children: [
17	          /* back arrow, title — unchanged */

28	
29	```dart
30	class _RecordsPageState extends State<RecordsPage> {
31	  bool _isOpeningExportSheet = false;   // NEW
32	
33	  Future<void> _openExportSheet(BuildContext context) async {
34	    if (_isOpeningExportSheet) return;                                   // FR-011
35	    _isOpeningExportSheet = true;
36	    final state = context.read<RecordsBloc>().state;
37	    final dateRange = state is RecordsLoaded ? state.dateRange : DateRangeOption.allTime;
38	    final bounds = dateRange.boundsAt(DateTime.now());                    // RF06's own pure extension, reused
39	    await showModalBottomSheet<void>(
40	      context: context,
41	      isScrollControlled: true,
42	      builder: (_) => ExportSheet(periodStart: bounds.from, periodEnd: bounds.to),
43	    );
44	    if (mounted) _isOpeningExportSheet = false;
45	  }
46	
47	  // build(): `_Header(onExportPressed: () => _openExportSheet(context))` replaces the bare `_Header()`.
48	}
49	```
50	
51	- `_isOpeningExportSheet` resets to `false` only after `showModalBottomSheet`'s `Future` resolves (the sheet
52	  was dismissed) and only if the widget is still mounted — a second tap while the sheet is open is already
53	  physically blocked by the modal barrier Flutter itself draws, so this flag's only real job is absorbing a
54	  double-tap in the brief window before the sheet has finished animating in.
55	- No change to `RecordsBloc`'s own filter state: reading `context.read<RecordsBloc>().state` here is a
56	  one-time snapshot at tap time, never a `watch` — `_Header` itself stays a plain, non-rebuilding
57	  `StatelessWidget` with respect to `RecordsBloc` (unaffected by RF05, same as `_SearchBar`'s existing
58	  `context.watch<RecordsBloc>()` usage for the filter icon's own highlight state, which this unit does not
59	  touch).
60	
61	## Test scenarios this contract owns
62	
63	| # | Scenario | Expected |
64	|---|---|---|
65	| 1 | `RecordsLoaded(dateRange: DateRangeOption.thisWeek)`, download icon tapped | `ExportSheet` is constructed with `periodStart` = this week's most-recent-Monday boundary, `periodEnd: null` |
66	| 2 | `RecordsLoaded(dateRange: DateRangeOption.allTime)`, download icon tapped | `ExportSheet` is constructed with `periodStart: null, periodEnd: null` |
67	| 3 | Download icon tapped twice in rapid succession (before the first `showModalBottomSheet` future resolves) | `showModalBottomSheet` is called exactly once |
68	| 4 | Sheet dismissed, download icon tapped again | `showModalBottomSheet` is called again (a fresh `ExportSheet`/`ExportBloc`, research.md R6) — not blocked by the now-`false` guard |
69	| 5 | Opening/closing the export sheet, at any of its states | `RecordsBloc`'s own state (`entries`, `dateRange`, scroll position via `ScrollController`) is bit-for-bit unchanged before and after (FR-010/SC-004) |
